2. Opposite party No.2 obtained an ex-parte decree of Tli.7,85,121/- for 3'd May, 2005 in Artha Rin Suit No.5 of 2005 against the opposite party Nos.3-5. The decree holder thereupon put the decree into execution on 15' July, 2001 in Artha Rin Execution Case No.509 of 2005 before the Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka for realization of the decreetal amount. The mortgaged property was ultimately sold in auction and the opposite party No.1 purchased the mortgaged property at Tk.9,50,000/-. The sale was confirmed and thereafter the writ of delivery of possession was also given. Thereafter the petitioner, a Sweater Factory who is in possession of the mortgaged property filed an application purported to be under Order 21 Rule 89 on 10' April, 2006 after complying the formalities for setting aside the sale on the ground amongst others that it is an export oriented limited company and the company had five share-holders, that the company had suffered huge loss due to stock lot and thereafter the promoter share-holders as a measure to recover its debt made an arrangement with Sonali Bank, that in pursuance thereof the company was reconstituted and some new share-holders had been inducted for raising equity with a view to meet the bank's liability and as a part of this arrangement, some shares were transferred to new share-holders with the approval of the bank and that they are bonafide purchasers for valuable consideration without knowledge of the mortgage of the suit property by the judgment debtors or the decree passed by the Court. 

 3. The Artha Rin Adalat allowed the application and set aside the said auction sale by judgment and order dated 24th April, 2006. The auction purchaser thereupon preferred Misc. Appeal No.164 of 2006 which was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, 7th Court, Dhaka who by judgment and order dated 30th October, 2006 allowed the appeal and reversed that of the Artha Rin Adalat. 

 5. The auction purchaser Mohiuzzaman Chowdhury is neither a decree holder nor a judgment debtor in the proceedings. He has participated in the bid as a stranger purchaser. Section 41(1) prescribed for filing an appeal by any party to the proceedings of the suit of the Artha Rin Adalat. The third party-petitioner's application for setting aside the sale was made under the provisions of Order 21 Rule 89 C.P.0 and the application was made in view of Section 26 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain which says the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure shall be applicable in execution proceedings if the provisions of AM is not inconsistent with the Code. Artha Rin Adalat though did not register the application as an independent miscellaneous proceeding. But it treated the proceeding as one under Order 21 Rule 89 C.P.C. and in that view of the matter, it ought to have registered an independent case number. At any event, in the appellate Court the learned District Judge treated it as a miscellaneous case and registered the appeal as Miscellaneous Appeal No.1 64 of 2006. This shows that the Artha Rin Adalat adjudicated the application as a Civil Court under the Civil Courts Act and not as Artha Rin Adalat. 

 7. We have heard the learned Advocates at length. We have also minutely read the words, the expressions, commas and stops used in Section 41, 26 and other provisions of the Artha Rin Ain. Sub-section (1) of Section 41 clearly provided that any person aggrieved by the order or decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat can prefer appeal in the manner provided in the said section. Admittedly, the auction purchaser is not a party to the proceedings. He is a stranger purchaser. If Sub-section (1), (2) and (4) are read conjointly, no interference other than that the right of appeal under this provision has been given to the decree-holder or the judgment debtor in the proceedings of the suit. In case of filing of an appeal by the judgment debtor he is required to deposit the 50% of the decreetal amount and in base of filing the appeal by the decree-holder financial organization, it does not require to deposit half of the decreetal amount. As auction purchaser he has already deposited the market value of the mortgaged property to the satisfaction of the Artha Rin Adalat and if again he is required to deposit the 50% of the decree amount, it will make no sense. In view of the above, the procedure for filing an appeal under this provision has been restricted to the decree holder or the judgment debtor and the use of expressions “কোন পক্ষ” cannot be extended to a third party who has accrued an interest or right in the subject matter of the decreetal property after passing of the decree who is not a party to the proceedings of the suit. 

 8. In case of passing an order or decree in a Artha Rin suit, if the decreetal amount is up to Tk.50,00,000/-, an appeal has been provided before the learned District Judge. But in case of an appeal other than the one provided in Section 41, as per provisions of the Civil Courts Act the District Judge has pecuniary jurisdiction to entertain an appeal against judgment and order of the learned Joint District Judge of a suit or proceeding which does not exceed Tk.5,00,000/-. Since the third party petitioner filed the application under Order 21 Rule 89 which having been allowed, an appeal is maintainable under Order 43 Rule 1 (j). In view of the above, we find that the learned District Judge acted illegality in entertaining the appeal and the learned Additional District Judge also in the same manner committed error of law in interfering with the order of the Artha Rin Adalat, since they have no pecuniary jurisdiction to entertain an appeal against a judgment or order passed by a Joint District Judge in respect of a proceeding over Tk.5,00,000/-. As we that the learned Additional District Judge had no pecuniary jurisdiction to hear the appeal, we are not inclined to enter into the merit of the matter. We find merit in the preliminary point raised by Mr. Mahmudul Islam. This Rule succeeds.
